info.title: OpenSpatialWorld API — OSL contract surface
info.x-osl-canonical-basis: Canonical schemas (World/User/View/Portal/Node/Spatial) and the /wow/world, /wow/user, /wow/view, /wow/portal and /wow/spatial paths are transcribed from the OPEN OpenSpatialWorld API (github.com/WebOfWorlds/WoWAPI, specification/OpenSpatialWorld/API.yaml, openapi 3.0.4, info.version 0.0.1), pinned to upstream commit d39a1a0 ("fixed node children type", 2026-05-21).
info.x-osl-provenance-correction: CORRECTION (2026-07-11, runtime; supersedes the previous claim here that this file was "NOT copied from the UNLICENSED simpleWorlds reference implementation"). That sentence was NOT supportable and is withdrawn. Two things in the first transcription match the STALE spec copy vendored in the simpleWorlds reference implementation rather than the open spec: (1) `Node.children` was typed `integer`, where the open spec says `$ref: Node` (simpleWorlds packages/wow-spec/src/schema.yaml:425-428 types it `integer`; upstream has ONE commit, so NO published upstream state has ever said `integer`); and (2) the dotted operationIds (world.getWorld, user.getUser, user.deleteUser, view.getView, portal.getPortal) match simpleWorlds 5-for-5, where upstream uses getWorldStatus / getUserById / deleteUserById / getViewById / getPortalById. Sourcing was MIXED, not wholesale: the /wow/spatial/{spatialID}/node/{nodeId} path is the OPEN SPEC's, and OSL deliberately REJECTED simpleWorlds' /wow/scene/node divergence (PROP §9). `Node` is now restored VERBATIM from the open spec. What OSL served then (id-ref children) was the LABELED, non-canonical `OSLFlatNode` divergence — declared, never presented as the standard. Since iteration 1 OSL serves the canonical `Node` by default and the flat form only on explicit request. NO simpleWorlds SOURCE CODE is vendored in this repository; the schema typing and operationId NAMING above are the extent of the overlap, and the typing is corrected. LICENSING NOTE: simpleWorlds' license state is self-contradictory — the repo ships an Apache-2.0 LICENSE file while its package.json (root and packages/wow-spec) declares "license": "UNLICENSED". Because that is unresolved, OSL treats simpleWorlds as DO-NOT-COPY and single-sources the open spec.
info.description:
OSL's typed, validated source of truth for the OpenSpatialWorld
("Web of Worlds") API. This is the contract every WoW-primary OSL
component builds against.

HONESTY / EXTENSION POLICY (binding, see wow-spec/OSL-WOW-CONTRACT.md):
  * CANONICAL surfaces carry the tag `canonical` and are transcribed from
    the open OpenSpatialWorld spec (WoWAPI@d39a1a0). Where OSL diverges
    from the standard, the operation/schema carries `x-osl-divergence` and
    the payload schema is a LABELED extension — NEVER a canonical one.
    (The known divergences are enumerated in OSL-WOW-CONTRACT.md §9.)
  * OSL ADDITIONS are ADDITIVE, carry the tag `osl-extension`, and every
    such schema/property is annotated `x-osl-extension: true`. They are
    NEVER canonical and MUST be surfaced (never hidden) by the conformance
    components.
  * `standards_conformance` stays `false` on every `/wow` response
    (validation-boundary honesty). No cosmetic conformance.
  * The WoW `Portal` schema has NO destination field; OSL carries a portal
    destination as a LABELED extension (`PortalDestination`).
  * `WS /events` is a LABELED non-canonical realtime convention,
    documented in the contract note, NOT in this HTTP contract.

Frames. All coordinates are in metres, right-handed, +Y up. A Spatial's GeoPose anchors its origin: at zero angles +X is east, +Y up and +Z south. All other positions are local to their parent.

servers.description: OSL local world-server node A (labeled local validation; not public)
OSL local world-server node B (labeled local validation; not public)

tags.name: canonical
tags.description: Transcribed from the open OpenSpatialWorld spec (WoWAPI@d39a1a0). Where OSL diverges, the operation/schema carries x-osl-divergence and the response is a LABELED extension schema — never a canonical one.

tags.name: osl-extension
tags.description: LABELED OSL addition where the WoW standard is silent. Additive, non-canonical, annotated x-osl-extension, surfaced by conformance.

get.summary: Returns a World status as a single data state.

200.description: world summary (canonical World + labeled OSL extensions)

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: ID of user to return (canonical domain is integer).

parameters.name: portalId
parameters.description: ID of portal to return (canonical domain is integer).

get.summary: Returns a Spatial (the graph id, the root node id and the GeoPose anchor of the graph).

parameters.name: spatialID
parameters.description: ID of the spatial composition graph. An integer. OSL also resolves the deprecated string aliases (world id, location id, 'default', 'world').

parameters.name: form
parameters.description: OSL EXTENSION. `descriptor` (default; alias `spatial`) returns the `Spatial`. `node` returns the graph's root node itself, as the canonical `Node` or, with the node form `flat`, as the `OSLFlatNode`. The served form is echoed in the `X-OSL-WoW-Spatial-Form` response header. Equivalent to the request header of the same name, which wins.

parameters.name: X-OSL-WoW-Spatial-Form
parameters.description: The request-header form of the `form` query parameter.

parameters.name: X-OSL-WoW-Node-Form
parameters.description: OSL EXTENSION. With `form=node`: `flat` returns the root as the `OSLFlatNode`; omitted or `canonical` returns the canonical `Node`.

200.description: The `Spatial` by default. With `form=node`, the root node, and the response header `X-OSL-WoW-Spatial-Form` says `node`.

get.summary: Returns a node of the spatial composition graph, with its whole subtree embedded.

parameters.name: spatialID
parameters.description: ID of the spatial composition graph (an integer; string aliases are deprecated).

parameters.name: X-OSL-WoW-Node-Form
parameters.description: OSL EXTENSION. `flat` returns the node as the `OSLFlatNode` (children are integer ids). Omitted, or `canonical`, returns the canonical `Node`. `?nodeForm=flat` is equivalent.

200.description: The node as the canonical `Node`; the `OSLFlatNode` when the node form is `flat`.

post.summary: Create and add new child nodes under the given parent node.

parameters.name: spatialID
parameters.description: ID of the spatial composition graph (an integer; string aliases are deprecated).

parameters.name: nodeId
parameters.description: ID of the existing parent node.

parameters.name: X-OSL-WoW-Node-Form
parameters.description: OSL EXTENSION. `flat` means the body is `OSLFlatNode[]` (leaf nodes only) and the response is every node stored, as `OSLFlatNode[]`. Omitted, or `canonical`, means the body is the canonical `Node[]`, whose children may be embedded to any depth; the server assigns every id and returns the nodes the caller sent, with their subtrees and the ids assigned.

requestBody.description: Array of new nodes to add as children of the parent. Canonical `Node[]` by default.

200.description: Successful operation: the created nodes as `Node[]`, ids assigned at every depth. The response header `X-OSL-WoW-Nodes-Stored` reports stored over sent.

400.description: OSL EXTENSION. `invalid_child_entry`, or, in the `flat` form, `child_id_refs_not_supported_on_create`.

422.description: Validation exception. A body that is not a valid `Node[]` (`node_validation_failed`), a `localTransform` that is not a placement (`invalid_local_transform`: wrong length, a last row other than 0,0,0,1, a number that overflows, shear or zero scale), or a graph that would be too deep (`node_tree_too_deep`). Nothing is stored.

put.summary: Update an existing node's content, or move it by setting `parent`.

parameters.name: spatialID
parameters.description: ID of the spatial composition graph (an integer; string aliases are deprecated).

parameters.name: X-OSL-WoW-Node-Form
parameters.description: OSL EXTENSION. `flat` means the body is an `OSLFlatNode`. Omitted, or `canonical`, means a `Node`.

requestBody.description: The updated node. `children` is derived from the tree: a PUT may leave it out or repeat it unchanged, and a PUT whose `children` differ from the stored ones is refused. A PUT of `parent` moves the node, with its subtree, under another node of the same graph.

200.description: Successful operation: the node as the canonical `Node`.

422.description: Validation exception. `child_restructure_not_supported` (the `children` sent differ from the stored ones), `invalid_local_transform`, or a refused move: `parent_not_found`, `parent_would_create_cycle`, `cannot_move_root`, `invalid_parent`, `node_tree_too_deep`.

delete.summary: Deletes a node and its subtree. Its ids are never issued again within the world.

parameters.name: spatialID
parameters.description: ID of the spatial composition graph (an integer; string aliases are deprecated).

400.description: Invalid node value, or the root, which cannot be deleted.

GeoPose.description: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Basic-YPR. `position` is latitude and longitude in degrees, and `h` in metres above the WGS-84 ellipsoid. `angles` are `yaw`, `pitch` and `roll` in degrees, applied about the local axes z, y and x in that order. `lan` is a deprecated spelling of `lon`: a reader accepts it and a writer sends `lon`.

lan.description: Deprecated spelling of `lon` (the World API at d39a1a0).

geoPose.description: The world's location, for discovery. It is not a placement: nothing inside the world is positioned by it.

id.description: Unique within the world, and never reused.

parent.description: The node this one is placed in. Every node has one parent, except the graph's root, which has none. A PUT of `parent` moves the node, with its subtree, under another node of the same graph; a move under the node itself or its own descendant is refused.

children.description: The child nodes, embedded. Derived from the tree: a PUT leaves them out or repeats them unchanged, and a PUT whose children differ is refused.

localTransform.description: Column-major 4×4 matrix mapping this node's frame into its parent's frame, in metres. It decomposes into translation, rotation and non-zero scale, with no shear, as glTF 2.0 §3.5.3 requires of `node.matrix`.

native_teleportxr_teleport.description: false in this version — no native TeleportXR session teleport.

first_party_teleportxr_browser_rendering.description: false in this version — not first-party TeleportXR rendering.

standards_conformance.description: false on every /wow response — no cosmetic conformance.

target_base_url.description: base URL of the destination world server.

spatial_fabric_address.description: loadable spatial fabric address of the destination.

SpatialFabricSubtree.x-osl-divergence: D8 — the WoW standard has no concept of a node that transcludes a SIGNED, EXECUTABLE spatial document. OpenSpatialAsset is media-type-plural (model/gltf-binary, model/vnd.usdz+zip, ...) but has NO signed-document type. This capability is OURS, labeled, and proposed upstream — it is not granted by the spec.
SpatialFabricSubtree.description: LABELED OSL EXTENSION — carried at `node.webofworlds_extension.spatial_fabric_subtree`. It is the CONTRACT behind the ADDRESS in `Node.spatialAssetURI`, and it is the DISCRIMINATOR: a node is a fabric node iff this member is present. The `.msf` suffix is NEVER sniffed — suffix-sniffing hides exactly the contract this object exists to state. FOUR REQUIRED FIELDS, and every one of them is required for a reason that has already bitten: (a) `unitsPerMeter` has NO DEFAULT. The fabric compositor's `auto` rule is "a fabric whose walk contains celestial nodes composes in AU; any other composes in its native metres". Inherited into a 1:1-metre WoW room, `auto` silently means 1 AU = 1 METRE. That is a defensible reading and a catastrophic default, so it is REFUSED, not defaulted (OSL-FAB-XFORM-1 §3). (b) `upAxis` has NO DEFAULT. The fabric corpus is Z-up; WoW/Three is Y-up. Guess wrong and the solar system lies on its side, silently. An absent or unrecognized `upAxis` is a REFUSAL (OSL-FAB-XFORM-1 §2 — the implementation refuses it, so this contract requires it; a contract that disagreed with its implementation would be the very disease this components is treating). (c) `placement` has NO DEFAULT. It SELECTS THE BACKEND, and the two backends make DIFFERENT HONESTY CLAIMS (see the property description). Defaulting would pick a claim on the author's behalf. (d) `fabricURI` is the signed document itself. NOTHING HERE EARNS A CONFORMANCE FLIP: `standards_conformance` stays `false`. The capability is labeled OSL, declared as divergence D8, surfaced by the conformance components — never disguised as canonical.

fabricURI.description: The signed `.msf` spatial fabric to transclude. NORMALLY IDENTICAL to the node's `spatialAssetURI` (which stays the WoW-native address). Resolved and then VERIFIED fail-closed by the existing `.msf` pipeline (`verifyMsfToken`) — an unverified, unfetchable or tampered fabric is REFUSED with a visible error at EVERY nesting level: never silently dropped, never drawn.

mediaType.description: PROVISIONAL, UNREGISTERED LABEL. `application/msf+jws` is the honest provisional name for a signed, executable spatial document. NO SUCH MEDIA TYPE IS REGISTERED WITH IANA — do not claim otherwise. Registering (or renaming) it is an upstream/MSF question, not ours to settle. Advisory only: it is NOT the discriminator (the presence of this schema is).

unitsPerMeter.description: REQUIRED. NO DEFAULT. EVER. World units per fabric metre (`k` in OSL-FAB-XFORM-1 §3). It is FOLDED INTO THE COMPOSITOR (`composeScale = k * s`, where `s` is the node's decomposed uniform scale) rather than post-multiplied — the engine's own (S·R)² light-intensity rule then applies for free and correctly. Worked example (the demo case): a tabletop orrery with 1 AU = 0.5 m in a 1:1-metre room is `k = 0.5 / 149597870700 = 3.3423e-12`. Omitting this field is a REFUSAL (`MISSING_UNITS_PER_METER`); a non-positive or non-finite value is `BAD_UNITS_PER_METER`.

upAxis.description: REQUIRED. DECLARED, NEVER SNIFFED, NEVER DEFAULTED. `z` = the fabric corpus default (the shared Sneeze UV sphere is Z-up), and the host inserts the fixed basis change B = R_x(-90°) — a pure isometry, determinant +1, so NO GEOMETRY IS RESHAPED. `y` = the fabric is authored Y-up and B = I. An absent or unrecognized value is a REFUSAL (`UNKNOWN_UP_AXIS`), never a fallback to `z` — a fallback would silently reintroduce the exact bug this field exists to kill (OSL-FAB-XFORM-1 §2).

placement.description: REQUIRED. NO DEFAULT. It SELECTS THE BACKEND, and the two backends make DIFFERENT, INCOMPATIBLE HONESTY CLAIMS — so an absent/unknown value is a REFUSAL (`UNKNOWN_PLACEMENT`), never a silent fallback to the flattering backend. `in-room` -> the THREE lowering: ONE scene graph, ONE depth buffer, so an avatar can walk in front of / behind / around the fabric and the occlusion is CORRECT. Shading is APPROXIMATE and it carries **NO PARITY CLAIM, EVER** (`render: "three-approx"`). `backdrop` -> the FILAMENT stacked layer: the measured-parity path (masked SSIM 0.941 vs Artemis's own capture), but it CANNOT DEPTH-COMPOSITE — two stacked WebGL canvases have no shared depth buffer (that is physics, not preference), so NOTHING IN THE ROOM CAN EVER OCCLUDE IT. `artemis.msf` is a backdrop and works perfectly as one; an in-room plinth-mounted fabric would be painter-ordered and an avatar could not walk in front of it.

parallax.description: BACKDROP ONLY. A LABELED dial, 0..1. `0` (the honest default) = orientation-locked: the backdrop follows the camera's rotation but not its translation, which is the truthful behaviour for a layer that has no shared depth buffer. Meaningless for `in-room` (which is genuinely depth-correct and needs no parallax fake).

requireVerified.description: FAIL-CLOSED BY DEFAULT. Absent or `true` => the fabric MUST verify (RS256 + x5c chain to a SHIPPED test anchor) or it is REFUSED and NOT DRAWN, keeping a labeled placeholder and a visible error. `false` is a LABELED local demo ESCAPE HATCH ONLY — it must never be set in a demo or a published world, and a world that sets it cannot claim its subtree is verified. NOTE: "VERIFIED" means a valid signature chaining to a shipped TEST anchor; it is NOT an OS-trust / public-PKI claim.

maxDepth.description: Per-subtree recursion cap for nested child fabrics (a fabric may transclude fabrics). ALWAYS CLAMPED by the engine's absolute MAX_DEPTH — this dial can only ever LOWER the cap, never raise it past the engine's own limit.

epochTicks.description: The epoch at which the fabric's `map.wasm` is run. Fabrics are TIME-DEPENDENT BY DESIGN (orbits move), so the epoch must be STATED rather than implied by wall-clock. This is also why the fabric's internal nodes are NOT projected back up into the WoW graph as addressable WoW nodes: any such projection is a SNAPSHOT AT AN EPOCH, not a graph (deliberately deferred).

allowed_entry_side.description: named against the portal frame forward axis.

OSLFlatNode.x-osl-divergence: Node.children: integer id-refs (OSL) vs embedded Node objects (canonical)

algorithm.description: MUST be "Ed25519" (the Profile A pair; never reinterpreted).

keyRef.description: did:key DID URL (offline-resolvable; consistency-checked vs the embedded key).

publicKeySpkiB64.description: base64 SPKI DER Ed25519 public key (the suite embedded-key escape hatch).

created.description: ISO 8601 (recommended). Lives inside the signature block; excluded from the signing input.

value.description: base64url (unpadded) Ed25519 signature over the JCS-RFC8785 signing input.

signature.description: UMSignature when signed; null on honest unsigned/unverified degradation.

open_user_manifest_label.description: Honesty label for open_user_manifest (real signature, non-canonical, standards_conformance:false).
